mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly compares parenchyma, collenchyma, and sclerenchyma tissues in terms of cell shape, wall thickness, and primary function?

options.A: Parenchyma cells are usually isodiametric with thin primary walls and are mainly involved in photosynthesis and storage; collenchyma cells are elongated with unevenly thickened primary walls providing flexible support; sclerenchyma cells are dead at maturity with heavily lignified secondary walls serving rigid support.
options.B: Parenchyma cells are dead with thick lignified walls; collenchyma cells are isodiametric with thin walls; sclerenchyma cells are living with flexible walls.
options.C: Parenchyma cells have thick secondary walls and provide rigid support; collenchyma cells are dead and store food; sclerenchyma cells are elongated with thin walls for flexibility.
options.D: All three tissues have similar thin primary walls and serve the same function of photosynthesis.

mcqs.answer: Parenchyma cells are usually isodiametric with thin primary walls and are mainly involved in photosynthesis and storage; collenchyma cells are elongated with unevenly thickened primary walls providing flexible support; sclerenchyma cells are dead at maturity with heavily lignified secondary walls serving rigid support.
mcqs.explanation: Option A accurately describes each simple permanent tissue: parenchyma – thin‑walled, living, versatile; collenchyma – living, unevenly thickened primary walls for flexible support; sclerenchyma – dead at maturity, heavily lignified secondary walls for rigid support. Options B, C and D contain incorrect combinations of wall thickness, living status or function, so they are wrong.

mcqs.question: All of the following are typical features of parenchyma cells EXCEPT:

options.B: They possess thick secondary walls impregnated with lignin.
options.C: They have thin, flexible primary walls.
options.D: They are involved in photosynthesis, storage, and wound healing.

mcqs.answer: They possess thick secondary walls impregnated with lignin.
mcqs.explanation: Parenchyma cells are living, have thin primary walls, and perform functions such as photosynthesis, storage, and regeneration. Thick secondary walls with lignin are characteristic of sclerenchyma, not parenchyma, making option B the only incorrect statement. Options A, C and D correctly describe parenchyma.

mcqs.question: Collenchyma tissue is best described as:

options.A: Dead cells with heavily lignified walls that provide rigid support.
options.B: Living cells with unevenly thickened primary walls that give flexible support.
options.C: Living cells with thin primary walls primarily involved in photosynthesis.
options.D: Dead cells with thick secondary walls that conduct water.

mcqs.answer: Living cells with unevenly thickened primary walls that give flexible support.
mcqs.explanation: Collenchyma cells are alive and have irregularly thickened primary walls, allowing them to support growing parts while remaining flexible. Option A describes sclerenchyma, C describes parenchyma, and D mixes characteristics of dead water‑conducting cells, none of which fit collenchyma.

mcqs.question: The primary function of sclerenchyma tissue in plants is to:

options.A: Conduct water and minerals from roots to leaves.
options.C: Provide rigid, mechanical support due to lignified walls.

mcqs.answer: Provide rigid, mechanical support due to lignified walls.
mcqs.explanation: Sclerenchyma cells become dead at maturity and develop thick, lignified secondary walls that give structural rigidity to stems, leaves and fruits. Options A and B refer to xylem and parenchyma respectively, while D relates to stomatal function, so they are incorrect.

mcqs.question: Complex permanent tissues differ from simple permanent tissues in that they:

options.A: Are composed of only one type of cell.
options.C: Consist of more than one type of cell working together for transport.
options.D: Are found only in animal bodies.

mcqs.answer: Consist of more than one type of cell working together for transport.
mcqs.explanation: Complex permanent tissues such as xylem and phloem are made up of two or more different cell types (e.g., vessels, tracheids, fibers, sieve elements, companion cells) that function together for transport. Simple permanent tissues consist of a single cell type. Options A, B and D are inaccurate.

mcqs.question: If a plant is placed in a dry environment, which permanent tissue primarily helps in upward movement of water to replace lost moisture?
mcqs.explanation: Xylem vessels and tracheids conduct water and dissolved minerals from roots upward, especially important when the plant needs to replace water lost by transpiration. Phloem transports sugars, parenchyma stores substances, and collenchyma provides flexible support, so they are not responsible for bulk water transport.

mcqs.question: Which of the following examples best illustrates the function of phloem in a flowering plant?

options.A: Transport of water from roots to leaves.
options.B: Movement of sugars from mature leaves to developing fruits.
options.C: Providing structural support to the stem.
options.D: Storing excess water in leaf vacuoles.

mcqs.answer: Movement of sugars from mature leaves to developing fruits.
mcqs.explanation: Phloem conducts organic nutrients, mainly sucrose, from source tissues (mature leaves) to sink tissues (growing fruits, roots, buds). Option A describes xylem, C describes sclerenchyma, and D is a function of parenchyma vacuoles, not phloem.

mcqs.question: A farmer notices that the stems of his wheat crop are stiff and break easily when wind blows. Microscopic examination shows a high proportion of thick‑walled sclerenchyma fibers in the stem. Which structural feature of these fibers explains the observed brittleness?

options.A: Presence of large central vacuoles that store water.
options.B: Unevenly thickened primary walls that allow flexibility.
options.C: Heavily lignified secondary walls that make the tissue rigid.
options.D: Thin primary walls that facilitate rapid growth.

mcqs.answer: Heavily lignified secondary walls that make the tissue rigid.
mcqs.explanation: Sclerenchyma fibers have thick, lignified secondary walls that provide rigidity but reduce flexibility, causing stems to become brittle and prone to breaking. Options A and D describe parenchyma traits, while B describes collenchyma, none of which cause the brittleness observed.
